subject: Inventory sprint charter, FedRAMP scope questions, and artifact request
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebank.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Cc: fed-audit@thirdparty-audit.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inventory sprint charter + FedRAMP scope questions

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we prepare the intake for our FedRAMP readiness engagement, the audit team asked us to confirm a few items up front so we can scope the artifact extraction window:

1) Sprint charter: can Redwood share a short-run sprint charter or intake plan that shows how you will collect and hand back evidence? We need owner names and a rough 2-week cadence if possible.
2) Control boundary sketch: the auditors want an initial diagram that shows the services in-scope (hosted API, Dedicated under tenant X, Private VPC stubs). A simple PNG is fine.
3) Data retention and snapshot cadence: please confirm current snapshot/retention windows for log and KV cache snapshots and any regional differences (us/eu).
4) SIG/CAIQ focus areas: do you have a prioritized list of control narratives you expect to deliver first?

Can we get these by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize the intake plan with the auditors? Attaching our intake template in case helpful.

Appreciate it —
Alice Morgan
Security Governance, Acme Bank

Attachment: acme-intake-template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebank.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, fed-audit@thirdparty-audit.com
Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inventory sprint charter + FedRAMP scope questions

Hi Alice —

Thanks — copying the core intake group. Quick answers and proposed plan below; I attached a draft sprint charter and a very rough control boundary sketch for comments.

A) Sprint charter / cadence
- Proposed sprint: 2 x 1-week sprints (intake + sample extraction), followed by a stabilization window.
- Owners: Jasmine Liu (comms / intake coordination), Olga Petrov (evidence routing / control narratives), Kimberly Park (audit logistics, retention confirmations).
- Deliverables per sprint: artifact index, control narrative drafts (SIG/CAIQ), sample snapshots, and a gating checklist.

B) Control boundary sketch
- Attached sketch highlights: hosted API (prod region us-west-2) + Dedicated tenant for Acme (logical isolation) + Private VPC (customer-managed). We have noted 3 external integrations: S3 backups (encrypted), KMS, and third-party logging.

C) Retention / snapshot cadence
- Logs: 90 days hot, 2 years archived (eu mirror follows GDPR controls). Snapshot cadence: daily log snapshots; KV cache snapshots truncated to customer TTLs for snapshot windows (we'll provide exact extraction commands).

D) SIG/CAIQ prioritization
- We'll prioritize control narratives for: identity & access, encryption in transit/rest, logging & monitoring, and incident response. Olga will own the first pass.

Next steps: Olga and Kimberly — can you review the attached sprint-charter-v1.docx and the sketch, and flag any missing owners or constraints? Alice — if this looks good I can finalize and share a Drive folder link for artifacts by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Technical Program Manager, Security Intake
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sprint-charter-v1.docx, control-boundary-sketch.png

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebank.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inventory sprint charter + FedRAMP scope questions

Thanks Jasmine — I reviewed the charter and sketched out the evidence extraction owners inline in the doc (high-level). A few clarifying notes: 

- Evidence extraction owners:
  * API telemetry (prod/us-west-2): Marcus Lin (infra) for snapshots & query access.
  * Dedicated tenant logs: Dedicated ops (we'll request access via the portal and provide a read-only artifact bundle).
  * KV cache samples: we will provide redacted samples and extraction commands; note that TTLs differ per customer so we should confirm Acme's retention requirement for sampling windows.

- Auditor ask: for FedRAMP scoping they want a short mapping (1-pager) showing how Redwood's artifact types map to FedRAMP control families (we can produce that).

- Risk flag: if Acme expects snapshots across multiple regions, there will be additional cross-region extraction lead time (estimate +3 business days).

I'll update the Drive folder and tag owners. Kimberly — can you confirm the retention confirmation for eu vs us snapshots?

-Olga
Senior Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebank.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inventory sprint charter + FedRAMP scope questions

Quick confirmation from retention side:
- Logs: us regions default to 90 days hot, archived to cold storage for 2 years.
- Snapshots: full environment snapshots retained for 30 days live, 180 days in object storage for audit sampling (can extend with DAL agreement).
- KV cache: not centrally retained beyond customer TTL by default — for audit we will take controlled extracted snapshots and redact PII per policy.

Kimberly Park
Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference

P.S. I added a small note to the charter about PII redaction steps and evidence labeling. Olga — please review before finalizing the mapping doc.

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

Alice —

Thank you. Finalizing next steps:
- I uploaded the sprint artifacts to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleSharedDrive (drive link above).
- Owners assigned in the charter (see sprint-charter-v1.docx).
- Olga to deliver FedRAMP mapping 1-pager by 2026-10-22.
- Kimberly to provide final retention confirmation and redaction checklist by 2026-10-21.

Proposed intake timeline: kickoff 2026-10-25, sprint 1 (intake + index) 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01, sprint 2 (sample extraction) 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08. Please confirm if the auditor needs a compressed artifact bundle or prefers Drive access.

For the auditors: if you prefer a JIRA work item for each control-family intake, we can create JIRA-SEC-721 and link artifacts there.

Best regards,
Jasmine
